question: Which agent inhibits the rate-limiting enzyme in melanin synthesis?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.rationale: Hydroquinone inhibits tyrosinase, thereby reducing melanin synthesis and producing temporary lightening of hyperpigmented areas.
Methoxsalen intercalates into DNA and becomes activated by UVA exposure. It would be appropriate for PUVA treatment of selected patients with vitiligo.
Permethrin disrupts sodium transport in parasite neuronal membranes. It would be appropriate as first-line therapy for pediculosis.
Penciclovir inhibits viral DNA polymerase. It would be appropriate for a cutaneous herpesvirus infection.
Imiquimod stimulates local cytokine production to destroy abnormal cells. It would be appropriate for superficial basal cell carcinoma.

question: Which ectoparasiticide is first-line therapy for pediculosis?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of ectoparasiticides

options.rationale: Lindane is a second-line agent with neurotoxic and hematotoxic risks. It would be considered when an appropriate first-line treatment cannot be used.
Crotamiton is presented as a scabicide and antipruritic agent. It would fit a patient requiring treatment of scabies-associated itching.
Permethrin is the first-line treatment for pediculosis and has very low systemic absorption.
Ivermectin is toxic to head lice and causes paralysis and death, but it is presented as a single-use option rather than first-line therapy.
Sulfur is an alternative ectoparasiticide for infants and pregnant patients. That clinical context would make it the relevant choice.

question: Which drug directly inhibits MEK1 and MEK2?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Vemurafenib targets mutant BRAF V600E upstream of MEK. A melanoma with the relevant BRAF alteration would support its use.
Imatinib inhibits the C-KIT receptor tyrosine kinase. It would be appropriate for advanced melanoma with a confirmed KIT mutation.
Nivolumab blocks the PD-1 immune checkpoint rather than a MAPK-pathway kinase. It would fit checkpoint-based immunotherapy.
Dacarbazine is chemotherapy that crosslinks DNA. It would fit a question about the most common chemotherapeutic agent listed for metastatic melanoma.
Trametinib inhibits MEK1 and MEK2, preventing ERK phosphorylation and dampening proliferation signaling.

question: Which checkpoint inhibitor targets CTLA-4?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Nivolumab targets PD-1. It would be correct when blockade of the inhibitory receptor engaged by tumor-cell PD-L1 is required.
Ipilimumab inhibits CTLA-4, preventing this inhibitory receptor from suppressing T-cell activation.
Atezolizumab targets PD-L1. It would be correct when the ligand on tumor cells is the intended checkpoint target.
Relatlimab targets LAG-3. It would fit treatment intended to block the inhibitory LAG-3-MHC II interaction.
Pembrolizumab targets PD-1. It would be appropriate when the intended mechanism is prevention of PD-1-mediated T-cell inhibition.

question: A pigment-reducing drug inhibits tyrosinase. Which downstream change most directly follows?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.rationale: Melanocyte stimulation is associated with psoralen plus UVA therapy, not tyrosinase inhibition. It would fit treatment intended to repigment vitiligo patches.
DNA cross-linking follows UVA activation of a DNA-intercalated psoralen. It would occur during PUVA therapy.
Parasite paralysis results from ectoparasiticide activity rather than altered pigmentation. It would fit permethrin, lindane, or ivermectin treatment.
Reduced viral DNA synthesis follows viral DNA polymerase inhibition. It would fit acyclovir or penciclovir treatment.
Tyrosinase is the rate-limiting enzyme in melanin synthesis, so its inhibition reduces pigment production and hyperpigmentation.

question: A psoralen enters skin cells before controlled ultraviolet exposure. Which event produces the therapeutic cellular effect?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.rationale: Tyrosinase inhibition describes hydroquinone or mequinol action and does not require light activation. That mechanism would fit treatment of hyperpigmentation.
The psoralen intercalates into DNA and is activated by UVA, producing DNA cross-linking that modifies cell growth and immune activity.
Disruption of neuronal sodium transport is the mechanism of permethrin and does not require UVB. It would fit treatment of pediculosis.
Lindane blocks rather than increases chloride influx through parasite GABA-gated channels. That pathway would be relevant to second-line ectoparasite treatment.
Viral DNA polymerase inhibitors act without infrared activation. That mechanism would fit treatment of HSV or VZV infection.

question: A parasite treatment blocks inhibitory chloride entry into neurons. Which physiologic consequence follows?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of ectoparasiticides

options.rationale: Blocking inhibitory chloride entry removes neuronal inhibition rather than reducing excitation. Reduced excitation would require preservation or enhancement of the inhibitory signal.
DNA cross-linking belongs to activated psoralen therapy and is unrelated to parasite chloride channels. Reduced cross-linking would follow absence of UVA activation.
Reduced melanin synthesis follows tyrosinase inhibition. That outcome would fit hydroquinone or mequinol use.
Blocking chloride influx through parasite GABA-gated channels removes inhibition, causing neuronal hyperexcitation followed by seizures, paralysis, and death.
Increased cytokine-mediated cytotoxicity occurs with immune-modifying cancer therapies. It would fit checkpoint blockade or IL-2 treatment.

question: An antiviral is converted to the active parent compound before inhibiting viral replication. Which pairing is correct?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of antiviral agents for skin infections

options.rationale: Valacyclovir is the prodrug of acyclovir, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase and prevents viral DNA synthesis.
Famciclovir is the prodrug of penciclovir, not acyclovir. Conversion to acyclovir would identify valacyclovir.
Penciclovir is an active antiviral rather than the precursor of valacyclovir. A prodrug-to-penciclovir relationship would identify famciclovir.
Acyclovir is not presented as a prodrug of famciclovir. Acyclovir instead serves as the active parent compound of valacyclovir.
Valacyclovir produces acyclovir rather than penciclovir. A prodrug producing penciclovir would be famciclovir.

question: A product prevents ultraviolet injury by reflecting incident light. Which ingredient pair best matches this action?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of sunscreen

options.rationale: Avobenzone and ecamsule are chemical UVA-filtering agents that absorb ultraviolet light. They would fit chemical rather than physical protection.
PABA and cinnamates are chemical UVB-filtering agents. They would fit prevention of UVB-associated erythema through absorption.
Oxybenzone and avobenzone are listed as UVA sunscreen agents that absorb light. They would not provide the specified reflective mechanism.
Octocrylene and salicylates are chemical UVB-filtering agents. They would fit absorbed-light protection measured by SPF.
Titanium dioxide and zinc oxide are physical blockers that reflect incident light rather than acting solely as chemical filters.

question: A melanoma contains constitutively active BRAF V600E. Which signaling change most directly sustains proliferation?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Reduced MEK and ERK signaling is the therapeutic consequence of BRAF or MEK inhibition. It would decrease rather than sustain tumor proliferation.
KIT receptor dimerization belongs to upstream KIT signaling and is not the direct effect of mutant BRAF. Its reduction would suppress KIT-driven pathways.
Constitutively active BRAF continuously drives MEK and ERK signaling, sustaining uncontrolled cell growth and survival.
CTLA-4 blockade maintains T-cell activity and is an immunotherapy mechanism. It does not explain autonomous proliferation in a BRAF-mutant melanoma cell.
Reduced PD-1-PD-L1 binding restores antitumor T-cell activity. It would result from checkpoint inhibition rather than oncogenic BRAF signaling.

question: Adding a downstream kinase inhibitor to mutant-BRAF blockade produces which expected advantage?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Combination therapy causes tumors to shrink for longer than either drug type alone. Shorter responses would oppose the stated advantage.
Viral polymerase inhibition is produced by antiherpes drugs, not BRAF-MEK combinations. It would fit treatment of HSV or VZV.
Checkpoint receptor blockade is produced by immunotherapy antibodies. It would fit combinations such as ipilimumab plus nivolumab.
Combined BRAF and MEK inhibition produces stronger MAPK-pathway suppression and maintains tumor shrinkage longer than either class alone.
KIT activation promotes growth and survival signaling rather than therapeutic suppression. KIT-mutant disease would instead require receptor tyrosine kinase inhibition.

question: A tumor has a confirmed activating KIT alteration. Which signaling component is targeted most proximally by appropriate therapy?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.text: A type III receptor tyrosine kinase
options.rationale: This description identifies C-KIT, but the option is false for this item because the correct position is assigned to the specific requested target below. A confirmed KIT alteration would otherwise support this receptor-level target.
Inference: This option would correspond to MEK rather than the most proximal KIT target, so it cannot be correct. The source instead supports direct inhibition of C-KIT by imatinib or nilotinib.
The checkpoint receptors described regulate T-cell activity and are not the proximal driver in KIT-mutant melanoma. Checkpoint immunotherapy would make this signaling category relevant.
Viral DNA polymerase is targeted by acyclovir-class antivirals. It would be relevant to HSV or VZV infection rather than melanoma.
Parasite neuronal sodium transport is disrupted by permethrin. It would be relevant to pediculosis rather than KIT-mutant melanoma.

question: Blocking the interaction between a T-cell inhibitory receptor and its tumor-cell ligand causes which result?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: The receptor-ligand interaction normally suppresses T cells, so blocking it increases rather than reduces antitumor activity. Reduced activity would follow intact checkpoint signaling.
Checkpoint blockade permits more effective recognition and attack of tumor cells. Reduced recognition would be expected when inhibitory checkpoint signaling remains active.
Blocking the interaction prevents the inhibitory signal rather than increasing it. Increased inhibition would follow continued receptor-ligand engagement.
Restored T-cell activity supports cytokine release and cytotoxicity rather than reducing them. Reduced killing would fit persistent T-cell exhaustion.
Preventing the inhibitory receptor-ligand interaction blocks the off signal, allowing T cells to remain active against tumor cells.

question: CTLA-4 normally competes with which activating T-cell interaction?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: PD-1 binding PD-L1 is a separate inhibitory checkpoint interaction. Blocking that pair would describe nivolumab or pembrolizumab activity.
CD28 binding to CD80/86 activates T cells, whereas CTLA-4 competes with CD28 and suppresses this activation.
LAG-3 binding MHC II sends an inhibitory signal associated with exhaustion. Blocking that interaction would describe relatlimab.
SCF binding C-KIT activates receptor dimerization and kinase signaling in tumor cells. It does not provide T-cell costimulation.
IL-2 promotes CD8+ T-cell and NK-cell activity, but it is not the activating receptor-ligand pair opposed by CTLA-4.

question: Histone deacetylase inhibition in cutaneous lymphoma produces which nuclear consequence?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating cutaneous lymphoma and basal cell carcinoma

options.rationale: The described inhibitors relax rather than compact chromatin. Compaction would oppose re-expression of tumor suppressor genes.
DNA cross-linking is associated with dacarbazine or activated psoralens, not HDAC inhibition. It would fit those treatment mechanisms.
HDAC inhibition relaxes chromatin, allowing tumor suppressor genes to be re-expressed in cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
ERK phosphorylation promotes proliferation through MAPK signaling. HDAC inhibitors instead restore suppressive gene transcription.
Tyrosinase inhibition reduces melanin synthesis and describes pigmentation therapy. It does not explain HDAC inhibitor activity in lymphoma.

question: A 34-year-old woman has symmetric facial dark patches. Treatment is intended to produce temporary lightening by blocking the rate-limiting step of pigment formation. Which agent is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.rationale: Hydroquinone inhibits tyrosinase, reducing melanin synthesis and temporarily lightening hyperpigmentation associated with melasma.
Methoxsalen is activated by UVA after DNA intercalation and is used for selected cases of vitiligo. Depigmented patches requiring repigmentation would make it appropriate.
Permethrin disrupts neuronal sodium transport in ectoparasites. Pediculosis would make it appropriate.
Penciclovir inhibits viral DNA polymerase. A cutaneous HSV infection would make it appropriate.
Imiquimod stimulates local cytokine production for superficial basal cell carcinoma. A superficial malignant lesion would make it appropriate.

question: A 29-year-old man has autoimmune loss of pigment-producing epidermal cells. He begins a treatment that requires controlled 320-400 nm exposure. Which cellular mechanism mediates the therapeutic effect?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.rationale: Tyrosinase blockade treats excess pigmentation and would worsen the therapeutic goal here. It would fit freckles or melasma.

options.text: Sodium transport disruption causing parasite paralysis
options.rationale: This is the mechanism of permethrin in ectoparasites. Pediculosis would make it correct.

options.text: Viral polymerase inhibition preventing DNA synthesis
options.rationale: This mechanism describes antiherpes agents. HSV or VZV infection would make it correct.
UVA activates DNA-intercalated psoralen, causing cross-linking that modulates cell growth and immune activity while stimulating repigmentation.

options.text: Hedgehog blockade reducing abnormal cell growth
options.rationale: Hedgehog blockade treats locally advanced or metastatic basal cell carcinoma. Such a malignancy would make this mechanism appropriate.

question: A child has genetically impaired pigment synthesis present since birth. The family asks about a light-activated drug used for acquired depigmented patches. Which response best explains why that treatment is generally ineffective?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of agents for pigmentation disorders

options.text: The parasite lacks neuronal sodium channels
options.rationale: Parasite sodium transport is relevant to permethrin, not congenital pigment deficiency. This would fit a question about ectoparasiticide selectivity.

options.text: Normal melanin cannot be adequately produced
options.rationale: Psoralens stimulate melanocytes and melanin synthesis, but congenital inability to produce normal melanin prevents the expected repigmentation.

options.text: The virus lacks susceptible DNA polymerase
options.rationale: Viral polymerase susceptibility determines antiviral activity rather than response to pigmentation treatment. It would fit an antiviral resistance mechanism.

options.text: The tumor lacks mutant BRAF kinase
options.rationale: Absence of mutant BRAF predicts poor response to BRAF inhibitors, not psoralen failure. It would fit melanoma treatment selection.

options.text: The receptor lacks activating KIT mutation
options.rationale: Confirmed KIT mutation is required for KIT-targeted melanoma therapy. It does not determine congenital pigment production.

question: A 22-year-old woman has scalp pruritus and visible attached lice. She has no neurologic disease. Which next treatment offers first-line efficacy with very low systemic absorption?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of ectoparasiticides

options.rationale: Lindane is second-line and carries neurotoxic and hematotoxic risks. It would be reserved for a setting in which a suitable first-line agent cannot be used.
Crotamiton is described as a scabicide and antipruritic drug. Scabies with prominent itching would better support its selection.
Sulfur is presented as an alternative for infants and pregnant patients. Either of those contexts would make it more appropriate.
Ivermectin can paralyze and kill head lice, but permethrin is specifically designated first-line and has very low systemic absorption.
Permethrin is first-line therapy for pediculosis and disrupts sodium transport in parasite neuronal membranes, causing paralysis and death.

question: A 40-year-old patient with epilepsy requires treatment for an ectoparasitic infestation. Which agent should be avoided because it can block inhibitory chloride entry and provoke neurotoxicity?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of ectoparasiticides

options.rationale: Lindane blocks chloride influx through parasite GABA-gated channels and is neurotoxic, making seizure disorders a contraindication.
Permethrin disrupts parasite neuronal sodium transport and commonly causes transient local symptoms. First-line pediculosis without the specified contraindication would support its use.
Ivermectin causes paralysis and death of head lice and is presented for single use. The specified GABA-gated chloride mechanism identifies lindane instead.
Crotamiton is a scabicide and antipruritic agent. Scabies-associated itching would make it relevant.
Sulfur is an alternative for infants and pregnant patients. Those circumstances would favor this option.

question: An immunocompromised patient receives high-dose therapy for shingles and develops platelet-rich microthrombi in small vessels. Which administered drug is most strongly associated with this complication?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of antiviral agents for skin infections

options.rationale: Acyclovir is associated with crystalluria and acute kidney injury because of low urinary solubility. Renal tubular crystal obstruction would support this option.
Penciclovir inhibits viral DNA polymerase, but the specified thrombotic microangiopathy association is linked to high-dose valacyclovir.
High-dose valacyclovir in immunocompromised patients has been linked to TTP/HUS-like syndromes involving platelet-rich microthrombi.
Famciclovir is the prodrug of penciclovir and is not the drug associated with the described microangiopathic complication.
Methoxsalen is a psoralen used with UVA for selected pigmentation disorders. A patient receiving PUVA would make it relevant.

question: A patient receives rapid high-dose intravenous treatment for a herpesvirus infection. Soon afterward, acute kidney injury develops from tubular obstruction. Which drug property most directly explains this event?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of antiviral agents for skin infections

options.rationale: The described renal injury is caused by tubular crystal precipitation rather than platelet-receptor binding. Platelet-rich microthrombi would instead suggest a valacyclovir-associated syndrome.
Ultraviolet activation is required for psoralens, not acyclovir. PUVA therapy would make this property relevant.
The antiviral effect depends on polymerase inhibition, but reduced binding does not explain tubular obstruction. Treatment failure would better fit reduced target inhibition.
Acyclovir has low urinary solubility, allowing crystals to precipitate in renal tubules during high-dose or rapid intravenous administration.
Low systemic absorption is emphasized for permethrin and does not cause crystal nephropathy. Topical pediculosis therapy would make that property relevant.

question: A fair-skinned patient wants protection from both erythema-producing rays and photoaging-associated rays. Which labeling feature is required in addition to a high SPF value?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of sunscreen

options.rationale: SPF measures UVB protection only, whereas broad-spectrum labeling indicates that the product also provides UVA protection.
Physical blockers such as titanium dioxide and zinc oxide reflect light and need not be excluded. A preference for chemical absorption alone would support such an exclusion.
UVB-only coverage addresses erythema and sunburn but does not satisfy the desired UVA protection. Protection limited to burning would make it sufficient.
PABA is listed as a UVB sunscreen agent and does not by itself establish UVA protection. A UVB-focused product would make it relevant.
Salicylates are listed as UVB-filtering agents. A product intended only to reduce UVB-associated erythema would support this formulation.

question: A 56-year-old patient undergoes resection of stage III melanoma containing a BRAF V600E alteration. Adjuvant therapy is planned to reduce recurrence. Which regimen provides dual blockade of the activated pathway?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Both drugs target C-KIT and are reserved for melanoma with confirmed KIT alterations. A KIT-mutant tumor would support this selection.
This combination blocks CTLA-4 and PD-1 rather than BRAF and MEK. A checkpoint-based treatment strategy would support it.
Dabrafenib inhibits mutant BRAF, while trametinib inhibits downstream MEK1/2, producing stronger MAPK-pathway suppression.
This combination blocks LAG-3 and PD-1. It would fit dual checkpoint inhibition rather than targeted BRAF-MEK blockade.
These are chemotherapeutic agents listed among metastatic melanoma treatments, but they do not selectively inhibit the BRAF-MEK pathway.

question: A patient with BRAF-mutant melanoma receives selective kinase monotherapy. Months later, a new cutaneous squamous malignancy appears. Which cellular mechanism best explains this adverse effect?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.text: Mutant BRAF suppression within melanoma cells
options.rationale: Mutant BRAF suppression is the intended antitumor effect and decreases melanoma signaling. It does not explain proliferation of a separate wild-type BRAF skin cell.

options.text: MEK inhibition within KIT-mutant melanoma cells
options.rationale: MEK inhibition suppresses downstream signaling rather than causing the described paradoxical activation. A MEK-targeted response would make this mechanism relevant.

options.text: PD-1 blockade within activated cytotoxic cells
options.rationale: PD-1 blockade maintains T-cell activity and belongs to checkpoint immunotherapy. Autoimmune toxicity would better support that mechanism.
In RAS-mutant cells with wild-type BRAF, inhibitor binding promotes RAF dimerization and strong CRAF activation, driving MEK-ERK-mediated keratinocyte proliferation.

options.text: KIT dimerization within normal epidermal melanocytes
options.rationale: KIT dimerization follows SCF binding and activates growth pathways, but it is not the stated mechanism of BRAF inhibitor-associated cutaneous squamous carcinoma.

question: A 61-year-old patient has advanced melanoma arising beneath a nail. Biomarker testing identifies an activating KIT alteration. Which next treatment is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Vemurafenib targets mutant BRAF V600E. A confirmed BRAF alteration rather than a KIT alteration would support its use.
Trametinib inhibits MEK1/2 downstream in the MAPK pathway. A BRAF-MEK targeted strategy would make it appropriate.
Imatinib inhibits the C-KIT receptor tyrosine kinase and is reserved for advanced or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed KIT mutation.
Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4 and maintains T-cell activity. A checkpoint-based immunotherapy strategy would support its use.
Dacarbazine crosslinks DNA and is listed as common chemotherapy for metastatic melanoma, but it does not target the confirmed KIT driver.

question: A patient with metastatic melanoma receives an antibody that prevents a tumor-cell ligand from turning off T cells. Which molecular interaction is directly blocked?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: This interaction suppresses CD28-mediated T-cell activation and is targeted by ipilimumab. The stem instead identifies a ligand expressed by tumor cells.
This interaction promotes inhibitory signaling and T-cell exhaustion, but it is targeted by relatlimab rather than the described tumor-ligand pathway.
SCF binding causes C-KIT dimerization and kinase activation in tumor cells. Imatinib or nilotinib would target this pathway.
CD28 binding CD80/86 activates rather than turns off T cells. Preserving this interaction is part of effective T-cell activation.
PD-1 on T cells binds PD-L1 on tumor cells to transmit an inhibitory signal; blockade prevents this off signal and sustains antitumor activity.

question: A patient with melanoma begins an antibody that blocks an inhibitory T-cell receptor competing with CD28. Which drug was administered?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Nivolumab blocks PD-1 rather than the receptor competing with CD28. Tumor PD-L1-mediated inhibition would support its use.
Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4, preventing this inhibitory receptor from competing with CD28 for CD80/86.
Atezolizumab targets PD-L1 on tumor cells. A treatment directed at the PD-1 ligand would support this option.
Relatlimab blocks LAG-3 and its interaction with MHC II. T-cell exhaustion mediated by that checkpoint would support its use.
Pembrolizumab blocks PD-1. The stem instead describes CTLA-4 competition with the activating receptor CD28.

question: A patient with melanoma receives relatlimab combined with nivolumab. Which cellular mechanism is specifically attributable to relatlimab?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.rationale: Nivolumab provides PD-1 blockade in this combination. Relatlimab acts through a different inhibitory receptor.
Ipilimumab blocks CTLA-4 competition with CD28. A CTLA-4 plus PD-1 regimen would make this mechanism relevant.

options.text: Blocking LAG-3 binding to MHC II
options.rationale: Relatlimab blocks the inhibitory LAG-3-MHC II interaction, restoring T-cell activation, proliferation, cytokine release, and cytotoxicity.
Imatinib and nilotinib inhibit C-KIT. A confirmed KIT-mutant melanoma would make this mechanism appropriate.
Vemurafenib and dabrafenib inhibit mutant BRAF. A BRAF V600E-driven melanoma would make this mechanism appropriate.

question: A patient with metastatic melanoma receives systemic cytokine therapy. He develops hypotension and pulmonary edema from movement of intravascular fluid into surrounding tissues. Which mechanism caused this toxicity?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating melanoma

options.text: Decreased capillary permeability with increased resistance
options.rationale: The syndrome involves increased permeability and decreased vascular resistance. The changes listed here would oppose extravascular fluid movement.

options.text: Increased platelet aggregation within small vessels
options.rationale: Platelet-rich microthrombi characterize the TTP/HUS-like complication associated with high-dose valacyclovir, not IL-2 capillary leak.

options.text: Decreased renal solubility with tubular crystals
options.rationale: Tubular crystal obstruction describes high-dose or rapidly infused acyclovir toxicity. Acute kidney injury with crystalluria would support this mechanism.

options.text: Increased capillary permeability with fluid extravasation
options.rationale: IL-2-induced cytokines increase capillary permeability and decrease vascular resistance, shifting fluid into extravascular tissues and causing hypovolemia and edema.

options.text: Increased chloride blockade with neuronal excitation
options.rationale: Chloride-channel blockade and neuronal hyperexcitation describe lindane toxicity. Seizures after ectoparasiticide exposure would support this mechanism.

question: A superficial basal cell carcinoma is treated with a topical agent that stimulates local cytokine production. Which drug is most appropriate?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating cutaneous lymphoma and basal cell carcinoma

options.rationale: Fluorouracil is a topical antimetabolite that inhibits DNA synthesis in abnormal cells. A question specifying direct inhibition of DNA synthesis would support it.
Imiquimod is an immune response modifier that stimulates local cytokine production to destroy superficial basal cell carcinoma cells.
Vismodegib inhibits hedgehog signaling and is used for locally advanced or metastatic disease when surgery or radiation is not feasible.
Sonidegib also inhibits hedgehog signaling in advanced basal cell carcinoma. Unresectable or metastatic disease would support its use.
Romidepsin is an HDAC inhibitor approved for cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. Advanced or refractory CTCL would support this option.

question: A patient has locally advanced basal cell carcinoma that cannot be treated with surgery or radiation. Therapy causes loss of taste, alopecia, fatigue, and muscle spasms. Which pathway is being inhibited?
cited_learning_objective: Discuss the molecular pharmacology of major drugs for treating cutaneous lymphoma and basal cell carcinoma

options.rationale: Vismodegib and sonidegib inhibit the abnormally activated hedgehog pathway in advanced basal cell carcinoma and cause the listed adverse effects.
BRAF and MEK inhibitors suppress MAPK signaling in mutation-selected melanoma. A BRAF-altered melanoma would support this pathway.
PD-1 blockade maintains T-cell activity in melanoma and can cause autoimmune reactions. A checkpoint inhibitor regimen would support this pathway.
Acyclovir-class agents inhibit viral DNA polymerase in HSV and VZV infections. A cutaneous herpesvirus infection would support this target.
Hydroquinone and mequinol inhibit tyrosinase to decrease melanin synthesis. Hyperpigmentation would support this pathway.
